claw_description: A Python AI agent connecting natural-language instructions with browser automation, spreadsheet operations, and local command execution through OpenRouter.
claw_overview: FakeOpenClaw explores how an AI agent can translate natural-language requests into executable actions. Users submit instructions through the terminal or Google Sheets; the Python agent consults an OpenRouter model, runs one command at a time, and returns each result to the conversation until the model provides a final answer.
claw_goal: The project demonstrates API integration, tool orchestration, browser control, and remote task input within a modular Python workflow.
claw_feature_input: Remote task input: receive prompts from the terminal or a polled Google Sheets cell.
claw_feature_ai: AI task planning: use OpenRouter to interpret requests and select the next shell, browser, or spreadsheet action.
claw_feature_browser: Selenium browser control: navigate pages, search Google, follow results, read visible page content, and capture screenshots.
claw_feature_sheets: Google Sheets operations: read ranges, update cells and ranges, append rows, clear data, and export CSV or JSON.
claw_feature_shell: Command execution: run terminal commands and pass their output back to the agent for subsequent decisions.
claw_feature_logging: Response logging: append timestamped AI replies to Google Sheets while feeding tool results back into the agent conversation.
claw_integrations: The project owner also describes LINE Bot and Google Apps Script integrations for remotely submitting instructions. These extend the messaging workflow; their implementation is not included in the published Python repository.
claw_technical_loop: Agent loop: main.py combines agent rules and tool descriptions into a system prompt. It parses COMMAND JSON or DONE responses, dispatches commands, and feeds execution results back to the model.
claw_technical_tools: Tool modules: sele.py handles Selenium browser actions, while google_sheet.py uses gspread and service-account authentication for prompt polling, spreadsheet operations, and reply logging.
claw_technical_validation: Command validation: the Python dispatcher validates command types and restricts spreadsheet tool actions to configured worksheet names. Parsing and execution errors are returned to the model for another decision.
claw_technical_stack: Technology stack: Python, Selenium, OpenRouter API, and Google Sheets API, with Git and GitHub for version control. LINE Messaging API and Google Apps Script support the owner-described messaging integrations.
claw_demo_description: Watch FakeOpenClaw in action and explore its remote AI automation workflow.
